messages:
maya: Heads-up — planning a per-tier canary for model-variant B in eu-west targeting mid-market hosted customers next week. Need clarity on fallback semantics, quota accounting, and telemetry naming. Sketch below.

maya: Plan: rollout variant B at 10% exposure for mid-market in eu-west for 48h. Dedicated/pinned customers excluded. If B is throttled or returns transient failures, fallback to variant A. Need to confirm: do we charge based on requested variant or served variant? How do we label telemetry so we can debug quality regressions?

dan: Quick Q: "per-tier" — is that strictly the customer_tier field on the request, or are we doing org-tags + tier? Also, what about region prioritization if a customer spans multiple regions?

maya: Scope = customer_tier (dev/pm/prod/mid-market/enterprise) + region. Org-tag can be used later. If a customer is multi-region, routing should prefer region match then global fallback. Dedicated customers are never part of hosted canaries — they stay pinned.

sophia: Two product concerns: 1) quota accounting when fallback occurs (we should bill for the variant actually served), 2) telemetry labels need to include served_variant, requested_variant, fallback_reason, and customer_tier so dashboards can pivot.

liam: For billing logic: charge for served_variant. If B was requested but A served due to fallback, bill A tokens. Charging B when A served creates reconciliation headaches.

maya: Agreed. Implementation note for runtime: emit these labels on each request: served_variant, requested_variant, fallback_from (if any), policy_path, customer_tier. Example event payload (schematic):
```
served_variant=B
requested_variant=B
fallback_from=B->A
customer_tier=mid-market
policy_path=tier_eu-west_10pct
```

dan: Also need routing priority tiebreakers when multiple policies apply (region vs tier vs global). Proposal: priority = customer_pin > tier_rollout > region_rollout > global_rollout. Thoughts?

sophia: That ordering sounds right. For the console UX, expose that priority as a tooltip in the rollout modal. Also show per-tier exposure numbers and a tiny note: "Fallback respects quotas and billing" with a link to advanced policy docs.

rollout-bot: Canary scheduled by maya for 2026-04-01 09:00 UTC. Trigger will create route entries and telemetry tags. /cc @oncall

maya: Implementation owners: I can own metrics + dashboard (served_variant, fallback_rate by tier/region). Need someone to add quota tests and make sure fallback doesn't bypass hard limits. Also someone to update routing priority in the runtime and ensure KV cache migration when switching variants.

liam: I'll add quota + e2e tests. I'll ensure fallback never bypasses per-customer hard token limits; if a fallback would exceed quota, we should return a 429 rather than switching variants silently.

dan: I'll take the routing priority PR and kernel-side handling for KV cache when swapping variants (we need a short migration window to warm cache to avoid latency spikes). I'll add a policy check in the router that refuses to route to an incompatible quantization-level variant for pinned customers.

sophia: Ops ask: add an alert that fires if fallback_rate > 2% for enterprise customers in any region over a 10m window. If sustained for 10m, trigger auto-rollback of exposure by halving the rollout for that tier. Also add a dashboard widget: fallback_rate by tier/region + top fallback reasons.

maya: Nice. One more telemetry naming ask: make labels consistent with existing naming conventions (snake_case) and include a boolean 'fallback_occurred'. Example metrics to emit:
- inference.served_variant
- inference.requested_variant
- inference.fallback_occurred (0/1)
- inference.fallback_reason (throttle|error|overquota|incompatible)
- inference.customer_tier

liam: Confirming test cases I'll add: (1) B returns 503 -> fallback to A and charge A; (2) B fallback would exceed tenant quota -> 429 and no fallback; (3) region mismatch -> route to nearest region variant then fallback globally.

dan: Also adding a light-weight canary telemetry tag in traces: rollout_exposure_percent and rollout_id so we can join traces quickly. We'll include that in the rollout API response headers for debug builds.

sophia: Console UX follow-ups: add a small "preview" table in the rollout flow that shows per-tier + per-region projected QPS and estimated cost delta for the exposure % so PMs can make decisions without digging into cost dashboards.

maya: Cool. Let's sync in 15 for a 10min alignment. After that dan/liam will pair on the PRs. :thumbsup:
